questions.q: What makes the checklist in this lesson a real security review tool rather than a list of good intentions?
options: It only applies to Meridian Trust Bank and no other instance
Each item is specific and checkable, traceable to a real platform setting or query — not a vague impression of security posture
It replaces the need for any ACLs on the instance
It is generated automatically by the platform with no manual review needed
questions.explain: A checklist's value comes from each item being verifiable against an actual setting (sys_user_role counts, Audit flags, SSO configuration), not a general feeling.

questions.q: After Lesson 23's remediation, which checklist sections did this three-lesson capstone leave unassessed at full depth, per this lesson?
options: Role design and field-level ACLs
Data protection/encryption coverage and security operations readiness
Authentication and SSO
Governance and audit logging
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states column-level encryption coverage, non-production data masking, and security-operations configuration were never assessed at the same depth in this capstone.

questions.q: Why does the lesson insist on stating that limitation plainly, rather than treating the capstone's three fixes as a complete review?
options: Because fixing three findings does not mean every section of the checklist has actually been verified — "we fixed what we noticed" isn't the same as "we reviewed the instance"
Because the checklist is optional and doesn't need to be run in full
Because Meridian's instance has no remaining risk after Lesson 23
Because the checklist only applies before any fixes are made, never after
questions.explain: The whole point of running the full checklist is to avoid mistaking a partial fix for a complete review.

questions.q: Why does a security review checklist need to be re-run on a schedule, rather than once?
options: ServiceNow deletes all roles and ACLs automatically after one year
A passing score is a snapshot, not a permanent state — new roles, ACLs, and fields get added over time, exactly how Meridian's original findings accumulated
Checklists expire and must be rewritten from scratch every year
Re-running the checklist is only necessary after a security breach has already occurred
questions.explain: Every one of Lesson 22's findings existed precisely because nobody had re-run a check like this one in four years.

questions.q: What specific risk does this lesson identify as the handoff to Course 11, ServiceNow DevOps, Testing & Deployment?
options: That a correctly designed secure configuration can still arrive broken, partial, or silently reverted when moved between environments without a disciplined promotion process
That DevOps and security are unrelated disciplines with no real connection
That Course 11 will re-teach ACL design from scratch
That production environments never need any security configuration at all
questions.explain: Configuration promotion across environments is a distinct risk from configuration design — getting it right once in sub-production doesn't guarantee it survives the move to production.
